What's in the ZIP

Every download is one folder named after the model. Inside you get:

FileWhat it is for
name.fbxThe model for Roblox Studio. Up to 4,000 triangles. Most models are already sized in studs; see Troubleshooting if yours is not.
name_tex.pngThe color texture for the FBX model (1024 × 1024 px).
name.glbA more detailed version for other 3D tools. It is not made for Roblox limits.
LICENSE.txtWhat you may do with the model, with your license key.
README.txtA short summary and a link to this guide.

For Roblox Studio you only need the .fbx and the _tex.png file.

Before you start

  1. Install Roblox Studio and sign in. Buttons may move a little in newer versions than the one named above.
  2. Open a place to work in. A new Baseplate place is enough.
  3. Unzip the download. The ZIP opens into a folder with the model name, and the files are in another folder with the same name inside it.

Importing uploads the model and the texture to the Roblox account you are signed in with (Upload to Roblox is on by default). Use an account you are happy to upload to.

Import the model

  1. On the Home tab, click Import. Do not use the Import button inside the Terrain Editor; that one is for height maps.
  2. In the file dialog, pick the .fbx file from the ZIP.
  3. The Import Preview window opens. The default settings are fine. Before you click Import, fix the texture as shown in the next section.

After the import, the Import Queue panel shows a green check, and a new Model with a MeshPart called Handle appears in Workspace. The model stands upright and faces the front.

Apply the texture

Most models show a base_color_texture row in Import Preview with a red mark: “Could not read the color map texture file associated with this object.” You can fix it right there.

  1. In the tree on the left, click base_color_texture (under world ⟩ Handle).
  2. Next to Color File Path, click the folder icon.
  3. Pick the _tex.png file from the ZIP. The row gets a check mark. Click Import.

Some models have no base_color_texture row at all and come in white. Add the texture after the import:

  1. On the Home tab, click Assets to open the Asset Manager.
  2. Click Import in the Asset Manager and pick the _tex.png file. In the Import Queue, click Start Import.
  3. When the green check appears, find the image in the Asset Manager and note its number in the ID column.
  4. In Explorer, select the Handle part of the model. In Properties, type texture in the filter.
  5. Click TextureContent, type rbxassetid:// followed by the ID (for example rbxassetid://1234567890) and press Enter.

Turn it into an accessory

  1. On the Avatar tab, click Accessory. The Accessory Fitting Tool panel opens.
  2. Click the Part field, then click the model in the viewport. The field shows Handle. Click Continue.
  3. Choose Accessory, then the accessory type from the table below. Leave Select Body Type as it is. A mannequin appears and the model moves to its place on it. Click Continue.
  4. The blue box shows the space the accessory may take. Click Generate MeshPart Accessory at the bottom of the panel.
  5. A small window says the accessory was generated into Workspace. It may open behind the main Studio window. Click OK.

The new Accessory is in Workspace and is named Handle, after the part. Rename it (for example KabutoHelmet) and delete the original imported Model, which has almost the same name, so you do not mix them up.

Model categoryAccessory typeWhere it sits
HatHatOn the head
HelmetHatOn the head
BackBackOn the back

Try it on a character

  1. On the Avatar tab, click Character. In Generate Rig, keep R15 and click Block Avatar (2012). A figure called Rig appears in Workspace.
  2. In Explorer, drag your accessory onto Rig. It snaps to its place without any moving by hand.

Use it in your experience

  1. Move the accessory to ServerStorage and give it a name without spaces, for example KabutoHelmet.
  2. In ServerScriptService, add a Script with the code below. Change the name in WaitForChild to yours.
  3. Click Play. Your character wears the accessory.
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage")

local accessory = ServerStorage:WaitForChild("KabutoHelmet")

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
	player.CharacterAppearanceLoaded:Connect(function(character)
		local humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid")
		humanoid:AddAccessory(accessory:Clone())
	end)
end)

Troubleshooting

ProblemWhat to do
The model is white or grey.The texture was not applied. See Apply the texture.
The model is much bigger than the character.Select the imported Model in Explorer, type scale in the Properties filter and set Scale to a smaller number (for example 0.3). Do this before the Accessory Fitting Tool.
Import opened a height map dialog.You used the Terrain Editor. Close it and use Home ⟩ Import.
The fitting tool does not pick the model.Click the Part field first, then the model in the viewport.
The “generated” window does not show up.It is behind the main Studio window. Move the main window or switch to it with the keyboard.

If a model cannot be used at all, see licenses and refunds.

Publishing

Selling or sharing an accessory on the Marketplace has its own rules, checks and fees, set by Roblox. Read Publish to Marketplace in the Roblox documentation before you try. Check also what your license allows.
